cold
June twenty twenty-four. A field team spends a week collecting surveys offline, on four tablets.
Before anything is uploaded, an app update logs them out of the project.
Three tablets are rescued by hand. The fourth never is.
problem
Every survey round ends the same way. Someone resets the tablets.
And the server's received count can't see what still lives only on the device.
A photo that never uploaded. A record stuck on the tablet. A spreadsheet that looks short, when nothing is missing at all.
brand
This is LastCopy. An agent that proves what's still on a tablet, before you wipe it.
zetaris
The evidence lives in four places that never meet.
Zetaris puts one SQL layer over all of them. No copying, no pipelines.
Seven queries in twelve seconds, and every suspicious record surfaces.
agents
Then the agents take over. A Meterless World Model plans every step.
NVIDIA Nemotron, through Nightshift, turns each suspicion into a hypothesis.
And a Reviewer sends weak ones back, before anything is fetched.
bytes
But models never decide.
Code compares the original bytes. Every record, every answer, every photo.
decide
Five tablets. One answer each.
Safe to wipe. Recover first, with the exact file named. Or hold, for a person.
adversary
Then it attacks itself.
An Adversary tries to break every clearance, with five objections.
Code must answer each one from the raw bytes, or the tablet is held.
proof
Every decision ships with a certificate anyone can re-check. Without LastCopy, and without a model.
blind
Is it only a demo? So we built blind tests.
Five hundred random fleets, with hidden problems the agents never see.
Nineteen hundred and eighty tablets. Zero wrongly cleared.
different
What makes LastCopy different?
It proves before you wipe. It argues with itself. And it holds up, blind.
close
LastCopy. Wipe a tablet only after its last copy is safe.
